title: Activity Selection Problem
statement:
You are given `n` activities. Activity `i` starts at time `start[i]` and finishes at time `finish[i]`, occupying the half-open time interval `[start[i], finish[i])`. A single person can attend only one activity at a time.

Two activities are **compatible** if one of them finishes no later than the other one starts (an activity that finishes at time `t` and another that starts at time `t` do not clash). A person may attend a set of activities only if every pair of them is compatible.

Return the **maximum number of activities** one person can attend.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
Each of the next `n` lines contains two integers `start[i]` and `finish[i]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the maximum number of pairwise compatible activities.

examples.explanation: Attend (1,3), then (4,7), then (8,10). No selection of four activities is compatible.
Each activity ends exactly when the next one starts, which is allowed.
The long activity (0,10) clashes with both short ones; skipping it lets you attend (1,2) and (3,4).

hints: Greedily choosing the earliest-starting activity or the shortest one can be wrong. Try to build a small counterexample for each.
Think about which activity, among all of them, leaves the most room for the rest of the day. It is the one that finishes first.
Sort by finish time, keep the finish time of the last chosen activity, and take each activity whose start is at least that finish time.
